display.title: Feeling for Others: The Rabbi Who Waited in the Cold
display.summary_short: A rabbi collecting for a freezing, penniless family makes a wealthy friend step out into a winter night, so he will truly feel what the poor feel.
display.summary_long: A short story from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. A famous rabbi is collecting tzedakah for a family with no food, no warm clothing and no firewood. He needs a large sum, so instead of visiting his generous wealthy friend by day as usual, he comes late on a freezing, stormy night and refuses to come inside. The butler argues, but the rabbi insists that the rich man come out to meet him just as he is. Puzzled, the rich man steps into the cold, and only then does the rabbi agree to enter. He explains that he wanted his friend to taste what it feels like to be poor and without warm clothing. The rich man thanks him for the lesson and gives everything the poor family needs.
display.lesson: To help others properly we must truly feel what they feel.
